issue.title: Receipt total is one cent higher than my calculator says
issue.body:
I'm trying out the cart with a 15% discount code. I add 2 x Notebook at 19.99.

Calculator: 39.98 minus 15% = 33.983, so 33.98.
Receipt prints:

    Notebook x2  $39.98
    Discount (15%)  -$5.99
    TOTAL  $33.99

So we charge a cent more than we should. It doesn't happen with 10% or 20% on round prices, only on some combinations. I suspect floating point somewhere in the total calculation.

Python 3.11, current main.

files.tests/test_cart.py:
from shop.cart import Cart


def test_plain_total():
    cart = Cart()
    cart.add('Pen', '1.50', qty=2)
    assert cart.total() == 300


def test_ten_percent_discount():
    cart = Cart(discount_percent=10)
    cart.add('Pen', '2.00', qty=5)
    assert cart.total() == 900

expected.cause: percent_off in shop/discounts.py truncates the per-line discount with int() instead of rounding it half up, so the discount is a cent too small and the total a cent too high.

notes: Symptom shows in the receipt/cart total; cause is in discounts.py. Reporter guesses floating point (wrong). README promises half-up rounding of discounts, so a good analysis may also note the doc/code disagreement.
